summary: Record the slot-lifecycle transition idiom (FOR UPDATE) in AGENTS.md
description:
**As** the team, **I want** the catalog slot-lifecycle **transition idiom** recorded in `AGENTS.md`, so US-009/US-011 (and every later slot transition) don't re-introduce the check-then-act race that AI-review caught in TKT-49.

**Priority:** P3
**Depends on:** — (documentation; TKT-49 is Done and is the reference implementation)
**Type:** Task · `risk:low` — a docs-only edit to `AGENTS.md`, no code.

**Background:** In TKT-49, the first archive implementation did a conditional `UPDATE ... WHERE status='published'` and then re-read status in a *separate* statement to decide whether to emit the domain event. A concurrent `draft→publish` could commit in between, producing a phantom `performance.archived` event on a still-published row (with a nil `archived_at` → mismatched deterministic id). Codex adversarial review flagged it [BLOCKING]. The fix: decide **and** transition inside one transaction with the row locked `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` (the same idiom as `services/access/internal/store/postgres.go` redeem). This is a promotable **technical learning** (metrics comment on TKT-49, learning #1) routed through a gated ticket per the '3 houses' rule rather than committed directly to the shared `AGENTS.md`.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] `AGENTS.md` gains a short note (a line or two, in the working-agreement/conventions area) stating: any catalog slot-lifecycle transition that both mutates state AND derives a to-emit decision must decide under `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` in one transaction; a conditional `UPDATE ... WHERE status=x` followed by a separate re-read is racy and can emit a phantom domain event.
- [ ] The note cites the reference implementations: `catalog ArchivePerformance` and `access` redeem.
- [ ] No code change; `make check` still green (docs-only).

Quality gates: `make check` green (docs-only, so trivially); no contract/UI surface.

binding.rule: Every admission-granting offer (performance, festival day, park operating day) is a dated slot in one inventory machinery; passes are entitlements to claim slot entries; lodging/day resources reserve through the same contention-safe core; slot attributes carry domain specifics — the claim primitive does not fork.

reference.summary: TKT-49 metrics comment — learning #1 (the promotable transition idiom); reference impl catalog ArchivePerformance + access redeem
PRD v1 — TKT-2 catalog stories (US-009/US-011 will add more slot transitions)

<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=summary -->
Created 2026-07-14 from the TKT-49 retro (learning #1). Promotes the FOR-UPDATE slot-transition idiom to the shared `AGENTS.md` via a gated ticket rather than a direct commit (3-houses rule: technical standard → shared registry through a PR). risk:low — docs-only. Reference impls: catalog `ArchivePerformance`, access redeem.

<!-- sdlc:stage=ready kind=claim -->
Claimed TKT-54. Selection: moved to Ready by the human; it is the only Ready ticket, P3 but zero blockers (TKT-49 — the reference impl — is Done), and it closes the loop on the TKT-49 AI-review [BLOCKING] finding before US-009/US-011 add more slot transitions.

Branch `TKT-54-slot-transition-idiom` created off `origin/main` (edc8000, includes US-009/TKT-51). Docs-only: a short note in `AGENTS.md`; no service code, no migration, no `make check` surface beyond the docs-trivially-green gate.

`risk:low` upheld — single-file docs edit (`AGENTS.md`), no auth/migration/CI-config, well under the 5-file threshold. → Planning.

<!-- sdlc:stage=planning kind=plan -->
**Plan — TKT-54 (docs-only, risk:low)**

**Deliverable:** one bullet in `AGENTS.md` under `## Working agreement`, recording the FOR-UPDATE slot-lifecycle transition idiom (TKT-49 learning #1).

**Text to add:**
> **Slot-lifecycle transitions decide under a row lock.** Any catalog slot-lifecycle transition that both mutates state *and* derives a domain event to emit must read the row `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` and decide + transition in one transaction. A conditional `UPDATE ... WHERE status = x` followed by a *separate* re-read is racy — a concurrent transition can commit in between and emit a phantom event (e.g. `performance.archived` on a still-published row, nil `archived_at` → mismatched deterministic id). Reference impls: catalog `ArchivePerformance` (`services/catalog/internal/store/postgres.go`) and access redeem (`services/access/internal/store/postgres.go`).

**Grounding (read real code):** the wording mirrors the actual TKT-49 impl at `postgres.go:264-309` (lock, switch on status, mutate + derive emit flags, single commit) and the `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` at access `postgres.go:190`. The phantom-event failure mode and nil-timestamp id mismatch are quoted from the TKT-49 code comment + ticket background, not invented.

**Satisfies ACs:** (1) states the rule + the racy anti-pattern; (2) cites both reference impls; (3) docs-only, no code, `make check` trivially green.

**Test seam:** none — docs-only, no runtime surface. Exit is the merged note.

**risk:low upheld:** single file (`AGENTS.md`), no auth/migration/CI-config. Next: codex cross-model critique of this note → plan-final → (Gate 2 skipped) Building.

<!-- sdlc:stage=plan-review kind=plan-final -->
**Plan-final — codex (gpt-5.5) cross-model critique folded in.** No BLOCKING; 2 SHOULD-FIX + 2 NIT, all accepted (they improve accuracy against the *current* code — US-009/TKT-51 added `CloseSlot`/`ReopenSlot`, both using the same FOR-UPDATE discipline, and `ArchivePerformance` now locks more columns).

**Triage:**
- [SHOULD] `access redeem` isn't a faithful equal — it's Access ticket-lifecycle, appends a lifecycle event (not a Catalog domain event), and its lock mainly makes duplicate scans idempotent. → Reframed as *the analogous row-lock decision pattern*, not an equal reference. (AC #2 still satisfied — both impls cited.)
- [SHOULD] Added the caveat: the tx decides + persists the transition and the owed-event markers, then **commits and emits at-least-once *after* the commit** — never publishes while holding the tx (matches the existing catalog emit/mark pattern).
- [NIT] Softened "must read the row `SELECT … FOR UPDATE`" — the real invariant is *decide from the locked current row in one atomic transaction*; `UPDATE … WHERE … RETURNING` is also safe. The racy form is specifically conditional-UPDATE + separate re-read to derive event state.
- [NIT] "slot-lifecycle" was too broad → "catalog slot state transitions that decide an owed domain event"; cite `ArchivePerformance` **and** `CloseSlot`/`ReopenSlot` (`toggleClosure`).

**Final AGENTS.md text (one bullet, `## Working agreement`):**
> **Catalog slot state transitions decide under a row lock.** Any catalog slot transition that both mutates state *and* derives an owed domain event must decide from the locked current row in one transaction — lock it (`SELECT … FOR UPDATE`), apply the transition atomically, then commit and emit the event *at-least-once after the commit* (the existing owed-marker pattern; never publish while holding the tx). A conditional `UPDATE … WHERE status = x` followed by a *separate* re-read to derive event state is racy: a concurrent transition can commit in between and emit a phantom event (e.g. `performance.archived` on a still-published row, nil `archived_at` → mismatched deterministic id). Reference impls: catalog `ArchivePerformance` and `CloseSlot`/`ReopenSlot` in `services/catalog/internal/store/postgres.go`; the same row-lock decision pattern underlies access `Redeem` (`services/access/internal/store/postgres.go`).

**risk:low → Gate 2 (plan approval) skipped.** Proceeding to Building (write the bullet, run `make check`, open PR).

<!-- sdlc:stage=coding kind=summary -->
**Building — docs-only bullet added to `AGENTS.md`.** PR #28.

One bullet under `## Working agreement` recording the FOR-UPDATE slot-transition idiom (TKT-49 learning #1), with the plan-review corrections folded in: reframed `access Redeem` as the analogous row-lock pattern (not an equal Catalog reference), added the emit-after-commit caveat, softened the SQL over-prescription, and cited the US-009 `CloseSlot`/`ReopenSlot` impls alongside `ArchivePerformance`.

**Gate:** `make check` green. **Diff:** docs-only (`AGENTS.md`), no code/migration/contract surface. Next: codex adversarial pass on the diff → needs:human.

<!-- sdlc:stage=ai-review kind=summary -->
**Building complete — codex (gpt-5.5) adversarial review done, finding folded in.** PR #28.

**Review triage (1 SHOULD-FIX, 0 BLOCKING, all accepted, fixed in-PR):**
- [SHOULD] The first wording over-claimed: it read as *any* catalog transition that mutates state + derives an owed event needs `FOR UPDATE`. But `PublishPerformance` (draft→published) also derives an owed event and deliberately uses a plain conditional `UPDATE ... WHERE status='draft'` — and that is correct, because a monotonic one-way transition's event id can't be invalidated by a racing opposite/terminal transition. Narrowed the rule to **state-deriving transitions where a concurrent opposite/terminal transition can interleave** (archive, close, reopen), and added an explicit carve-out naming `PublishPerformance` as the safe monotonic case.
- Everything else verified accurate: `ArchivePerformance`, `CloseSlot`/`ReopenSlot` (via `toggleClosure`), and access `Redeem` are named correctly and do use row locks as described; the phantom-event / nil-`archived_at` failure mode matches the code comments + the `archive_race_smoke_test.go` regression test.

No blocking findings survive; no incidental backlog tickets spun off (the one finding was a precision fix to the note itself). **Tooling note:** the ai-review codex run hung at "Reading additional input from stdin…" for ~5m with the prompt passed as an argument; killed and re-ran once feeding the prompt via stdin redirect (`codex … < prompt`), which completed cleanly — see retro.

`make check` re-run green after the fix. Spike-adjacent but not a spike: docs-only, no CI surface beyond the gate.

**→ needs:human (Gate 3).** Review-guide posted on PR #28. Stopping; no further pushes.
